title: Egg substitute, omelet, scrambled or fried, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Egg substitute is a ready‑to‑use blend that lets you make omelets, scrambled eggs or fried dishes without using real eggs and without added fat. It typically contains plant proteins, starch, flavorings and sometimes B‑vitamins to mimic the taste and texture of eggs.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Egg substitute is a staple in vegan cooking as an alternative to chicken eggs.
The blend can be based on soy, pea or hemp protein.
Some brands add turmeric or natural colorants to give a yellow hue similar to yolk.
It is shelf‑stable in dry form; preparation only requires adding water.
Using the substitute helps reduce cholesterol and saturated fat intake.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: The mix provides a complete amino‑acid profile, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Cooking without added oil keeps the dish low in calories.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Added B12, B2 and folate help replicate the nutritional value of eggs.

items.title: Heart‑friendly
items.content: Absence of cholesterol and saturated fats makes it safe for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Allergy‑friendly for egg‑allergic individuals
items.content: People with egg allergy can safely use the product.

items.title: Soy or pea protein allergy
items.content: Some substitutes are soy‑ or pea‑based and may trigger reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Missing micronutrients
items.content: Unlike real eggs, the product may contain lower amounts of vitamin D and choline.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Certain brands add salt for flavor; check the label if you need to limit sodium.

items.title: Texture variations
items.content: Improper water‑to‑mix ratios can result in a dry or overly runny final product.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Combine the substitute with water according to package directions (usually 1 tsp mix + 120 ml water). Pour the batter onto a pre‑heated non‑stick pan without oil and cook like a regular omelet or scrambled eggs until set.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the dry powder in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from moisture and direct sunlight. Once opened, use within about 6 months.
